newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: EIB escudo euro-option bond seen first of series.
newsitem.headline: EIB escudo euro-option bond seen first of series.

text.p: The European Investment Bank (EIB) may follow Thursday's launch of escudo bonds carrying a euro-option with issues in other currencies, but the move says nothing about Portugal's chances of qualifying for the single currency, a senior EIB official said.
Carlos Ferreira da Silva, Luxembourg-based coordinator of EIB strategy for the euro, told Reuters in a telephone interview that the issue had been made for "strictly financial reasons."
"We need funds and there being a market opportunity, we made the issue," he said.
"This issue implies no judgement over the likelihood of a particular currency taking part in the euro. These issues are open to all European Union currencies," he added.
Ferreira da Silva said that the 20 billion escudo, 10-year deal could be followed by issues in other currencies. He gave no further details.
"The EIB is preparing its debt for the advent of the euro and further issues in other (European Union) currencies should follow," he said.

The escudo issue, the first in a currency not widely regarded as certain to form part of a future single currency, can be redeemed in euros if Portugal enters the single currency which is due to be launched on January 1999.
So far such issues have been limited to currencies which analysts regard as being core to monetary union, such as the French franc and the Dutch guilder.
The escudo financing will pay annual interest of 5.75 percent and be repaid on February 15, 2007.
Ferreira da Silva noted that the issue contained a clause that allowed for its redemption in euro in the event of the escudo getting into the single currency, but only in this case.
Once switched into euros, the issue could be consolidated with other issues already made in the European currency or with the same option for convertion, he said.
"This is going to give us a liquid yield-curve in euros," he said.
